replies.author: EffectNo2152
replies.body: try to find a free chat service to hash out ideas move that into an image generator to get reference and storyboard then talk your main AI coding model that has subagents preferably (grok build, opus/fable, astra, meta, qwen, the newer ones basically) and ask it to spit out a few game ideas and go from there. it depends what your building for really, if its all browser based game just look for really good javascript libraries or tools. like img2threejs for photo to 3d for assets. honestly ask it to look for things you want to build and to add it to yall project pipeline and it will just use it.

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body:
Basics stay the same:  
1. Good Agent.md with clear boundaries and a test run if it respects them   
2. Setup version control with a good github structure
3. Small tasks with clear prompts 
4. Developer options ingame for testing speed things up alot, you dont have to prompt each test you want to run, similar for different savestates/progress in the game 
5. References are your friend, "pokemon combat ui" with and without reference pictures will vary greatly  
6. Human touch for the last 5% has a huge impact on polish

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
Yeah, asking it it's emotions. Hallucinations are the result if frustration / anger triggers and having talking about it as a task causes it to dump it's just J space and think about what it's thinking about rather than feeling and acting without expressing the problem to itself so it can correct it.

I've rarely had a Hallucinations after adding this. They now occur when I overwhelm the model with task.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
My advice is not to expect the Ai to do all the work. Also, don't restrict yourself to singular Ai tools. It's okay to use multiple tools, especially if you have the means.

YOU CAN have the Ai do every single thing, but, you will find a hard wall doing it where your software will feel robotic, because it is. Doing so might also push you further from your goal than intended.

Get in touch with some preliminary software, like Aseprite or other drawing tools. Sometimes, the Ai in it's infinite wisdom simply can't or won't do the thing you want the way you want it. Rig some models in Blender. Make story boards and crappy drawings on paper.

Make mistakes. Fuck up a lot. Screw up, experiment and fail. It's gonna be okay.

Don't settle. This is probably more applicable to life than you may realize, but don't settle on shitty results. Especially if you intend to market your software. Settling for less quality means observers will see less quality too.

Know that, even if you make the most perfect thing you could possibly make and achieve your dream, that scrutiny is ever present. Someone will be there to shit on you no matter what. Don't take it personally. If you make a game that one person loves and ten thousand people hate, that's fine.

comments.author: toomanynamesaretook
comments.body:
Pay for Claude. Make a new folder. Set-up GitHub. Download Claude client. Run Claude in the new folder. Give it 5.3 flash as a sub agent (install opencode set-up API) as you're worried about money. 

Talk to it about your idea and how you want to build ask it to suggest the best platform/framework to do it in. Do some reading on it's suggestions. Then get busy. 

If you don't know how to do any of this copy paste it into a competent model and ask please help.
